slots.purpose: The product's name, as spoken and as the wordmark. Reference wordmark: one word, ~12% of frame height.
The part of the name drawn in the second wordmark colour (e.g. 'Motion'); empty for a one-colour wordmark.
The product's mark (SVG preferred). The only logo in the film. Becomes the mark_src variable.
On-screen line under the wordmark in the reveal. Reference measured 48 chars, readable ~4 s.
VO only. The pain, in short sentences. Reference: 3 sentences in 17 s (15% of runtime).
The jobs that pile up around the persona in act 1. Reference bubbles ran ~50 chars and were unreadable at 720p; budget is set for video scale.

Optional. The spoken word in the problem lines each chip pops on, in chip order, '|'-separated (one plain word per chip that the transcriber hears as written). Empty = chips spread over the lines' stressed words. Chips never arrive on a timer.
VO: 'Meet <name>. <what it does>.' Must contain the name; the lockup lands on it.
The word the lockup lands on, plus '|' aliases for how the transcriber hears an invented name (e.g. 'Tidyslot|Tidislot|Tidy').

VO: one sentence per feature beat. Must contain its verb at least 0.7 s after the sentence starts (about 3+ words in). Reference: 10–25 words at ~124 wpm, median shot 6.5 s. End the line on a stressed word that comes after the action's result: the scene's exit starts on the last stressed word (J-cut).
The word in each beat line that names the action. The cursor's press lands on its onset (±0.25 s gate).

What the cursor does on the verb. select = tile/row gets selected; click = button press with a visible result; toggle = switch flips; type = field is clicked and text types in (and a mirror preview updates).
The real control the action hits (tile title, button label, toggle label, field). Must exist on the real screen.
Feature chip on the brand field, top-left, naming the feature for silent viewing. Reference chips: 'SEO', 'Social Media'.

Optional, one per beat: the kinetic keyword ({text, word} in beats[].keyword). Big display type on a white slab along the bottom, word-by-word waterfall, last word in the brand colour ('Pick a spotlight.'). Enters on `word` (default: the beat's verb; '|' aliases for numbers, e.g. 'nine|900'). Must echo the line and land >= 0.6 s before the beat's exit starts.

The product's real screen for each beat, redrawn at video scale as a screen spec: kind tiles | rows | toggles | editor | stages | player, with its real titles, labels, nav and status. Never a third-party UI.
The product's real sidebar navigation (sidebar chrome).
The product's real step names (stepper chrome), if its flow is a stepper.
VO: '<short opener>. <name>. <verb phrase>.' The name must come >= 1.2 s after the CTA cut and the verb >= 0.9 s after the name.
The word the CTA lockup lands on, with '|' aliases like reveal_name_word.
The word in cta_line the cursor presses the CTA pill on.
CTA pill label: a real call to action the product supports. Reference: 'Get Started Today' + URL.
The product's real URL. Leave empty rather than guess a domain.
Small end-card note (e.g. 'Sample product…', 'Concept film…'). Empty for a shipping product.
The brand's own mascot (transparent PNG) for the problem persona and the CTA cloud. Empty = initials avatars only. Never stock faces.
Shown in act 1 when there is no mascot.
Initials for the CTA people cloud (illustrated stand-ins for customers; never real people's names or faces).
Soft page ground behind the cards (brand kit canvas).
THE brand colour: the full/part-bleed field, shapes, chip text, selection ring. White text on it must pass AA.
Second brand tone: shapes, toggles-on, focus ring.
Primary text.
Secondary text (must pass AA on white; muted web greys usually fail).
The product's real primary button fill.
Text on the primary button.
Hairlines and borders.
Inner tile / row fill.
Status pill / badge fill.
Text on soft fills; row tags.
Success tick.
Dark preview-frame bezel.
Wordmark main colour.
Wordmark accent colour (wordmark_accent).
UI face (bundled OFL files).
Wordmark / preview-headline face (bundled OFL files).
Local Kokoro voice for `hyperframes tts`, read at speed 1.1 (voice_speed). af_heart measured the widest pitch range of the voices tried.
Kokoro speed multiplier.

Optional overrides for the pacing clock: gap_in_act (0.25-0.4 s, default 0.3), gap_between_acts (<= 0.6 s, default 0.45), tail (default 1.2 s), jcut_lead (0.04 s), beat_snap (0.15 s), result_hold (0.35 s), late_cut_max (0.25 s). Out-of-range gaps print a PROBLEM.
A bed the caller owns or licenses (~120 BPM, no drops). Ducked 7 dB only under words (attack 50 ms, release 150 ms) so it fills every gap; cuts snap to its beats (hyperframes beats) within ±0.15 s.
